newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suspected anti-atom activists halt German railways.
newsitem.headline: Suspected anti-atom activists halt German railways.

text.p: Suspected anti-nuclear activists halted rail traffic on two major routes in north Germany on Wednesday and forced hundreds of trains to be rerouted, police said.
A train driver was injured in two sabotage attacks, the latest protest against nuclear waste consignments to a depot at Gorleben, 120 km (75 miles) from Hanover.
Activists have sought to block rail traffic in the area several times in the last two years.
Saboteurs draped grappling hooks on overhead cables on two busy routes bringing power lines down, a spokesman for the railway police said.
The driver of a goods train on the Hamburg-Bremen route was was taken to hospital with injuries sustained when the cables smashed into his windscreen.
Full service was due to be restored later on Wednesday.
A goods train on the Hamburg-Neumuenster route also smashed into hooks draped on the cables but no-one was injured and power lines were quickly repaired.
Saboteurs carried out three similar attacks on railway lines in north Germany earlier this month. Another transport of spent nuclear waste to Gorleben had been planned next month.

But Gerhard Glogowski, interior minister of the northern German state of Lower Saxony, where the Gorleben nuclear waste depot is located, said this week the next shipment would be postponed until next year.

The state could not afford another massive police operation to protect another nuclear shipment to Gorleben this year, he said, arguing that his state should not have to shoulder the financial burden of such an operation alone.

When the last nuclear shipment was delivered in May, 19,000 police officers were mobilised across Germany -- 7,500 from Lower Saxony alone -- and the usually-peaceful farmland around Gorleben looked as though it had been hit by a civil war.
